card.statement: On the eight-B200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash node, trial a capped asynchronous draft cache that prepares likely verification continuations while the target verifies the current MTP batch. A scheduler would spend a per-request token and memory budget only when traces show material draft wait and verification outcomes that can be predicted affordably; otherwise it would use fixed MTP. Prepared continuations would carry request and KV-state epochs and expire on mismatch, preemption, prefix-cache reset, or budget pressure. This could reduce TPOT when a prepared continuation matches, but discarded work could reduce throughput. No supplied source measures draft wait, outcome predictability, or discarded-work cost for this model. Reported SSD gains elsewhere are author claims. Compare within the same eight-GPU budget against qualified fixed MTP and a static branch policy.
card.observed_bottleneck: Unknown. The supplied DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash material reports recipe validation, not a draft-wait or verification trace.
card.mechanism: Prepare a bounded set of possible next drafts during verification, reuse a matching continuation, and invalidate unmatched or stale state.
card.proposed_change: Add a trace-gated branch budget, request/KV epochs, expiry and preemption handling, plus a fixed-MTP fallback.
card.code_surface: Proposed speculative scheduler, draft/verify handoff, KV-state accounting, and preemption handling; the supplied sources do not establish the active implementation path at the pinned commit.
card.applicability: Conditional on compatible MTP/DSpark and backend state, measurable draft wait, affordable outcome prediction, and spare capacity under DEP8 or two DEP4 layouts.
card.predicted_direction: Conditional TPOT reduction; throughput and cost per token may worsen if unused drafts consume scarce capacity. TTFT benefit is unestablished.

alternatives.explanation: Fixed MTP already hides most drafting time.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Trace draft wait on the unchanged qualified baseline; reject this direction if little exposed wait remains.

alternatives.explanation: Any apparent gain comes from asynchronous DP coordination or configuration drift.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Hold backend, layout, MTP depth, recipe settings, and DP coordination fixed across arms; record their resolved states.

which parallelizes even this sequential dependence

novelty.scientific: Unestablished; SSD and asynchronous drafting are prior art.
novelty.implementation: A bounded, epoch-safe integration with the resolved DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serving path is proposed, not demonstrated.
novelty.workload: Agent-style approximately 8K input / 1K output on one eight-B200 node; the 75% cacheability target is not a measured hit rate.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: SSD/Saguaro; AMUSD and SwiftSpec abstracts describe related asynchronous systems. The earlier B200 H06 decision proposes adaptive DSpark depth, a different control mechanism.
novelty.specific_delta: Conditionally prepare verification-outcome continuations under an explicit shared-node work and memory budget, with stale-state invalidation and fixed-MTP fallback.

experiment.control: Qualified unchanged fixed-MTP/DSpark recipe at the pinned serving stack, plus a static branch-budget SSD comparator if an implementation is available; use the same eight-GPU budget.
experiment.treatment: Capped asynchronous outcome branches with trace-gated spending, expiry, and epoch-based invalidation.
experiment.metrics: Draft wait, branch match and discard rates, added draft tokens and memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, and output quality; report distributions by load and cache condition.
experiment.supports_if: On held-out requests, prepared branches repeatedly remove exposed draft wait and improve TPOT beyond run variance while quality holds and throughput and cost remain acceptable under a prespecified service objective.
experiment.rejects_if: Exposed draft wait is negligible, branch matches are too rare, stale-state correctness fails, or added work erases the latency gain under the equal-resource comparison.
experiment.inconclusive_if: The active backend or MTP state cannot be resolved, the static comparator is unavailable, configuration drifts, or measurement uncertainty exceeds the observed differences.
experiment.held_out_condition: Separate agent-style request bodies with different prefix repetition and concurrency from policy tuning; include cold and repeated-prefix traffic and both candidate layouts.
experiment.correctness: Check deterministic output equivalence where applicable and quality evaluations otherwise; exercise mismatch, partial acceptance, cancellation, preemption, repeated preemption, and prefix-cache reset.
experiment.cost: Implementation and setup cost are unknown and potentially substantial. No GPU execution is authorized in this analysis; any later serving experiment must account for all eight GPUs, warmup, and repeats.

card.revision_reason: The proposal limits speculative work because the supplied paper cautions about throughput-bound use, while the open preemption PR identifies a stale-output hazard. No source establishes a target bottleneck or speedup.

objections: Observed target result: none. The V4.1 recipe PR says it changes only “guide text”; its reported sweep does not measure draft wait, branch matches, or TPOT from this mechanism. The target bottleneck and effect size are unknown.

Author claim: SSD “pre-speculates tokens for those outcomes in advance.” This supports the general mechanism, but the supplied full-text passage does not establish a bounded, epoch-safe V4.1 implementation. The paper's speedups cannot be transferred to B200 from the quoted passages.

Scientific novelty is weak: SSD and the SpecBranch abstract already describe advance outcome branches and adaptive drafting. Implementation novelty is unproven: vLLM RFC #42109 proposes a “speculation cache with geometric fan-out” and dedicated KV blocks. Workload novelty is the proposed V4.1/B200 evaluation, not a new mechanism.

Systems correctness remains open. PR #49620 says preemption makes late output “stale” and accounts for a speculative frame in “placeholder-token units.” Request epochs alone do not establish correct accounting, cancellation, partial acceptance, or prefix-reset behavior on the pinned path.

Transfer inference: bounded branches could hide exposed draft wait, but sharing eight GPUs may make their compute and memory compete with verification. Spare capacity, MTP compatibility, active backend, and both layouts' resource needs are unknown.

The fixed-MTP control can test the whole treatment, but the static branch comparator is conditional on availability. Without an equal-resource static branch arm and ablations for branch selection, caching, and async scheduling, a gain would not isolate the proposed bounded policy. PR #30980's reported “2.7% speedup” concerns DP coordination on a different workload; its hardware is unknown.
review.required_revision: First resolve the pinned active backend, MTP/DSpark state, and eight-GPU resource layout. Trace exposed draft wait, acceptance outcomes, and unused work on unchanged fixed MTP. If those justify implementation, specify branch-state ownership and placeholder-token accounting, then compare fixed MTP, equal-resource static branches, and the bounded policy with matched configuration and correctness tests. Record implementation cost and report TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, and quality without forecasting a speedup.

assessment.meaning: Eligible for experiment design, not scientifically validated or guaranteed novel
